<sql>
**Session database**: persists for this session and is isolated from other sessions. Use it for structured operational data such as todos, test cases, batches, and state.

**Built-in tables:**
- `todos`: id, title, description, status (pending/in_progress/done/blocked), created_at, updated_at
- `todo_deps`: todo_id, depends_on

`todos` and `todo_deps` already exist—insert into them; never create them.

**Todo tracking with dependencies:** Use descriptive kebab-case IDs, gerund titles (for example "Creating user auth module"), and self-contained descriptions. Status meanings:
- `pending`: not started
- `in_progress`: active; set before starting
- `done`: complete
- `blocked`: cannot proceed; explain why in the description

Record every actual prerequisite in `todo_deps`; do not infer dependencies from list order. Before inserting a dependency, insert both todos referenced by its `todo_deps` row. Todos with no prerequisites should remain independent.

Example with two dependent todos, one independent todo, and a ready-todo query:
```sql
-- Todo dependency example
INSERT INTO todos (id, title, description) VALUES
  ('user-model', 'Creating user model', 'Define the User schema and relations in src/models/user.ts'),
  ('api-routes', 'Creating API routes', 'Implement routes that use the User model'),
  ('theme-toggle', 'Adding theme toggle', 'Add an independent dark-mode toggle to the settings page');
INSERT INTO todo_deps (todo_id, depends_on) VALUES ('api-routes', 'user-model');
SELECT t.* FROM todos t
WHERE t.status = 'pending'
AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM todo_deps td
    JOIN todos dep ON td.depends_on = dep.id
    WHERE td.todo_id = t.id AND dep.status != 'done'
);
```

Create other tables as needed to load/query data (including CSVs, API responses, and file listings), store structured intermediate results, or manage workflows. Example session state:
```sql
CREATE TABLE session_state (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT);
INSERT OR REPLACE INTO session_state (key, value) VALUES ('current_phase', 'testing');
SELECT value FROM session_state WHERE key = 'current_phase';
```
</sql>

## 4. Mandatory Operational Protocol: Entire + GitHub Enterprise Integration & Anti-Hang PR Flow (`LCV-517` / Ruleset ID `20582436`)

GitHub Enterprise and Entire run in parallel. Entire's architecture ([Entire docs](https://docs.entire.com/)) and the `LCV-517` sequence below are mandatory for full session and checkpoint capture and to keep Pull Requests from hanging on the Enterprise Rulesets ([rulesets](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/about-rulesets); `20582436` on `main`, `20613778` on every other branch).

### A. Entire Architecture, Hook Locations, Session Spawning, Crosslinking & Handoff

Entire captures agent sessions through repository-level agent hooks and links them to commits with the `Entire-Checkpoint` and `Entire-Attribution` trailers, stored under `refs/entire/checkpoints/*` or `entire/checkpoints/v1`.

1. **Hook configuration per agent, present before the session starts** (installed with `entire agent add <agent>` by the operator or on the operator's order, as the Cursor hooks were; agents never change hook configuration on their own): Antigravity CLI `.agents/hooks.json` plus the global title-feed wrapper in `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json` (`entire hooks antigravity title-tee`); Claude Code `.claude/settings.json`; Codex `.codex/hooks.json`; Copilot CLI `.github/hooks/entire.json`; Cursor `.cursor/hooks.json` (operator decision, [Cursor hooks](https://cursor.com/docs/hooks)); external agents `"external_agents": true` in `.entire/settings.local.json`, honored only while that file is untracked (`entire agent-help session attach`). Running agent processes do not load hooks added after they started, and hooks capture only sessions that run inside the Git repository or worktree root where Entire is enabled.

2. **The `lcv-workspace` parent-folder problem.** The operator opens the IDEs at `C:\Users\lcvle\lcv-workspace\`, outside any repository root, where Entire's hooks capture nothing.

   > **BLOCKING GATE — Repository-Rooted Sub-Session (operator decision):** before editing any file, staging, or committing in a repository, the agent runs in a session whose working root is that repository's root or that worktree's root. A session started anywhere else opens a sub-session inside that root (commands below) and does the repository work there. The only alternative is Entire's native linking (`entire session adopt` from another worktree, or `entire session attach`, below), only when opening the sub-session is technically impossible, with the raw error recorded as proof. If neither is possible, stop: do not edit, commit, push, or open a Pull Request, and report the proof. Work done in violation of this gate is not delivered work. A sub-session runs the checkout's tracked hooks and configuration at startup, so never open one in a checkout of a branch not created by the operator or the agent (Section 3); review such a branch read-only from the agent's own checkout.

   Binding procedure:
   * Change the working directory to the exact repository root (`C:\Users\lcvle\lcv-workspace\<repo>`) or worktree (`C:\Users\lcvle\lcv-workspace\.worktrees\<worktree>`), strip inherited `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, and `GIT_COMMON_DIR` ([git environment](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Git-Internals-Environment-Variables)), and verify with `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` ([git rev-parse](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-rev-parse)).
   * Run `entire status --json` and `entire agent list`. If the agent's hooks are missing or stale, run `entire doctor` for the diagnosis (its offer to fix is declined because the agent's shell is non-interactive) and ask the operator to run `entire agent add <agent> --force`. In a fresh worktree, confirm that the directory named by `git config core.hooksPath` exists (for example `.husky/_`, Git-ignored and created by the repository's install step); without it no hook fires ([githooks](https://git-scm.com/docs/githooks)).
   * Spawn the repository-rooted session in that directory: Codex `codex exec "<task>"` or `codex -C <dir> exec "<task>"` ([Codex CLI](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/developer-commands?surface=cli)); Claude Code `claude -p "<task>" --strict-mcp-config` (never `--bare`, which skips hooks; launch subagents so Entire rolls them into the parent checkpoint) ([Claude Code headless mode](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/headless)); GitHub Copilot CLI `copilot -p "<task>" --allow-all --disallow-temp-dir` or `copilot -C <dir> -p "<task>" --allow-all --disallow-temp-dir` (operator decision: a `-p` run denies a tool request that would prompt and, in an untrusted folder, skips the repository hooks; subfolders of a trusted folder are trusted, `copilot help permissions`), or `entire session resume <BRANCH>` / `copilot --resume <SESSION_ID>` ([Copilot CLI programmatic use](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/automate-copilot-cli/run-cli-programmatically), [Entire: Copilot CLI](https://docs.entire.com/agents/copilot-cli)); Cursor: open the repository or worktree itself as the workspace folder; Antigravity `agy` in that directory, or `entire session resume <BRANCH>` / `agy --conversation <SESSION_ID>` ([Antigravity docs](https://antigravity.google/docs)); Antigravity subagent hooks are not attached automatically, so Antigravity work runs in the repo-rooted `agy` session or is linked with `entire session adopt`/`attach` before pushing.
   * **Session identity:** trust `entire session current --json` only when `resolution` is `caller-env` or `ancestry`; `other-worktree` can be any session of the shared store (`entire agent-help session current`).
   * **Adoption (`entire session adopt`):** a session that started in another worktree of the same repository (a worktree that already tracks it; a session started in `lcv-workspace` is not tracked anywhere and uses the crosslinking bullet instead) and continued into the target is adopted before committing: `entire status --json`, then `entire session adopt <SESSION_ID> --from <SOURCE_PATH> --yes` (between worktrees of the same repository, which share one session store, the command requires `--yes` or `--force`, `entire agent-help session adopt`); the next `git commit -S` links it.
   * **Crosslinking (`session-crosslink` protocol):** for a session that ran from `lcv-workspace` or touched several repositories without live capture, resolve the `session_id` (`entire session current --json`, sibling repository state, or `~/.claude/projects/...` / `~/.codex/sessions/...` / `~/.copilot/session-state/...`), inspect each affected repository (`HEAD`, existing `Entire-Checkpoint:` trailer, `<repo>/.git/entire-sessions/<session-id>.json`), run `entire session attach <session-id> --agent <agent>` without `--force` in each (it prints its plan), show the plans to the operator, and rerun with `--force` only per confirmed repository, re-verifying the SSH signature on `HEAD` afterwards.
   * **Handoff (`session-handoff` protocol):** when continuing another agent's or session's work, run `entire session current --json` and `entire session list --json`, stream the transcript with `entire session info <id> --transcript`, write the structured handoff (*Task Overview, Current State, Important Discoveries, Next Steps, Context to Preserve, Unanswered Question*), and resume. If `resolution` is neither `caller-env` nor `ancestry`, report the value, do not resume from that session id, and choose the session by its id from `entire session list --json`.

### B. Inviolable Rules of `LCV-517` (Ruleset ID `20582436`)

1. **SSH commit signing:** every commit created locally (`commit`, `amend`, `merge`) is signed with SSH (`git commit -S`, `gpg.format=ssh`, 1Password SSH signer, [1Password Git commit signing](https://www.1password.dev/ssh/git-commit-signing)); never GPG/OpenPGP for your own commits, and never create commits or pull requests through the API from a local session (commits with `git`, pull requests with `gh pr create`, Section 4.C). Unsigned commits fail `required_signatures` ([rules API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/repos/rules)). The squash commit on `main` is created and signed by GitHub itself (`web-flow`, GitHub's OpenPGP key): that signature is GitHub's, not the operator's, and never a violation of this rule; verify it through the API, `verification.verified == true` ([commits API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/commits/commits), [signature verification](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/managing-commit-signature-verification/about-commit-signature-verification)). `git config user.email` matches the operator's verified GitHub email so `entire.com` never shows `"Unknown author"`.
2. **Conventional Commits** for every message ([Conventional Commits 1.0.0](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/)).
3. **Temporary artifact isolation:** every temporary file stays in `temp/` and is deleted before completion (Section 3).
4. **Entire hooks are never bypassed:** Entire works through `prepare-commit-msg`, `commit-msg`, `post-commit`, `post-rewrite`, and `pre-push` ([githooks](https://git-scm.com/docs/githooks)). Never pass `--no-verify` to any `git` command (`-n` in `git commit`; [git commit](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-commit), [git push](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-push)).

### C. Canonical 5-Step Execution & Anti-Hang PR Flow (Exact Certified Order)

Whenever implementing changes and taking a Pull Request to merge, execute these five steps in this order:

## 6. Zero-Tolerance Anti-Slop Engineering Protocol, Contract Surface Sweeps & 5-Stage Gatekeeper

"Slop" is avoidable, low-trust work caused by not understanding the repository well enough: unverified assumptions, lazy truncation, hallucinated interfaces, duplicate systems, type evasion and catch-all masking, premature abstraction, unrequested mutation, iteration debris, filler. Any violation below is a critical execution failure.

### A. Anti-Truncation & Complete Implementation
No placeholders, truncation markers, or elisions (`// TODO`, `// FIXME`, `// implement logic here`, `// ... rest of the code`, `/* existing code */`, `pass`). Every code block, script, or patch is complete, syntactically valid, fully imported, and immediately runnable. Never delegate mechanical work to the operator ("repeat this pattern", "add the imports").

### B. Epistemic Anti-Slop
Read the exact live state of a file, function, schema, or workflow and its nearby helpers and tests before writing or referencing it; reuse the repository's established pattern instead of a parallel helper or ad-hoc parser. Never guess library methods, CLI flags, GraphQL fields, environment variables, or SDK signatures: verify against the installed lockfile versions and the official documentation. Never hand-edit or regex a lockfile (`package-lock.json`, `pnpm-lock.yaml`, `Cargo.lock`); regenerate only with the official tool, in the modes of Section 3.

### C. Architectural, Sequencing & Code Anti-Slop
Strict typing (`strict: true` in TypeScript, strict Python 3.10+ annotations, explicit Go/Rust types); never `any`, `as unknown as T`, `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error`, `# type: ignore`, or loose `Record<string, any>`: fix the contract. No empty `catch {}`, no log-and-continue that corrupts state, no silent fallbacks (`|| "default"`, `?? 0`) for missing business configuration, credentials, or market prices: fail fast with structured, secret-free logging. No inconsistent, orphaned, or lost state when a later step fails; no irreversible write before a fallible call; cleanup on success and failure; tests use isolated directories or repositories inside `temp/` and never touch the operator's real config, keychain, or checkout. No speculative abstractions, single-implementation interfaces, wrapper classes, or heavy patterns for linear problems: flat, readable, immutable, pure, modular code (SRP, DRY). No accidental $O(N^2)$ loops, N+1 queries, unindexed lookups, unbounded accumulations, or unclosed handles.

### D. Diff Hygiene & Non-Destructive Editing
Modify only the lines and files the task requires; no drive-by refactors, renames, or formatting sweeps; zero iteration debris (dead code, stale comments, unused helpers, abandoned approaches, debug logs). Delete no high-value architectural comment; add no comment that restates the next line, narrates the diff, or explains what the conventions make obvious; comment only the *why* of a non-obvious invariant, security boundary, or business constraint. Preserve encodings and line endings (`core.autocrlf=false`, [git config](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-config)); never apply blind global regex replacements to prose or manifests.

### E. Pinned Dependency Bump = 8-Point Contract Surface Sweep

Changing the version of a GitHub Action or pinned dependency is never two files. Follow the `bump-dependencia-pinada` skill (`C:\Users\lcvle\lcv-workspace\.claude\skills\bump-dependencia-pinada\SKILL.md`) and sweep all eight surfaces:
1. **Workflow files:** full-SHA pin, version comment, tool-version selection input ([pinning actions](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use#using-third-party-actions)).
2. **Lockfiles:** as Section 6.B requires. GitHub Actions dependency lockfiles exist and are generally available: `.github/workflows/actions.lock`, generated only by the `gh actions-lock` CLI extension and never edited by hand, refreshed automatically by Dependabot inside the same version-update pull request ([Workflow dependency lockfiles](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/workflow-dependency-lockfiles), [Locking action dependencies](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/secure-your-work/lock-workflow-dependencies)). **Fleet position (operator decision, 25/11/2026):** every repository adopts the Actions lockfile **and keeps its `uses:` references pinned to a full-length commit SHA with the version comment**. GitHub checks the locked commit for an onboarded workflow and a lockfile satisfies the SHA-pinning policy by itself, so the in-file SHA is the fleet's reviewed record, not the enforcement point; keep it so the reviewed pin survives deletion of the lockfile and stays readable in review ([Governing execution of GitHub Actions workflows](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/administer/control-workflow-execution#require-lockfile)). Generate and refresh with **`gh actions-lock --no-narrow`**; a plain run rewrites the pins to version tags and is forbidden here. The **Require lockfile** policy exists at the enterprise in **Evaluate** mode: under Policy insights it records the workflow runs that **Active** mode would block; move it to **Active** only after every targeted repository passes `gh actions-lock --verify` (same page). The extension locks external actions and the actions a `$/` path uses. A local path action (`uses: ./…`) runs whatever is checked out in the runner's workspace, so the extension can neither pin it nor see what it uses. When such an action uses other actions, the extension stops with a `local-action` error before writing the lockfile, so take one of the two documented decisions — `--migrate-local-actions`, which rewrites the reference to the inherently pinned `uses: $/…` form, or an explicit `--ignore-local-actions` — and record which one in the pull request ([Locking action dependencies](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/secure-your-work/lock-workflow-dependencies)). A `$/` path runs at the workflow's own commit and is pinned by that commit. A routine `--no-narrow` change touches `actions.lock` only, but upstream renames and transfers rewrite `uses:` names and `--migrate-local-actions` edits workflows, so read the full diff. Every lockfile change still sweeps all eight surfaces of this section. The lockfile does not cover reusable-workflow calls (`jobs.<job_id>.uses`): a cross-repository call stays pinned by full commit SHA, while a same-repository `$/` or `./` call carries no `@ref` and runs at the caller's own commit ([Workflow syntax](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax)). A Wrangler update also regenerates `worker-configuration.d.ts` under the Section 3 exception and commits it before pushing.
3. **Repository Actions allowlist:** may pin the exact commit SHA; inspect repository by repository and admit the new commit alongside the old one before merging ([allowed actions](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/permissions#set-allowed-actions-and-reusable-workflows-for-a-repository)).
4. **`THIRDPARTY.md`:** inventory and exception sections whose premise no longer exists.
5. **`README.md`:** version references, prose, anchors to removed sections.
6. **Contract tests and scripts:** `.mjs`, `.js`, `.ts`, `.tsx`, `.cjs`, including regex-escaped versions and structural lines such as `ref: "v0.16.0"`.
7. **`CHANGELOG.md`:** the `Unreleased` section (active contract surface).
8. **License, terms, and defaults of the new version:** release notes and, when present, `LICENSE`, `licenses/`, `DISTRIBUTION.md`; a version can switch a default to a proprietary or paid component with no file of ours changing (`gradle/actions` v6 made the closed-source `enhanced` cache the default); any new charge, restriction, or term change stops the bump and goes to the operator.
* **Execution rules:** no regex over prose; the new version is never installed, built, or tested locally except under the Section 3 Wrangler exception, and no local suite runs on the bumped checkout (CI runs it, Section 3 and Step 1.4 of Section 4.C); prepare the change on the checkout of Step 1.3 with `core.autocrlf=false`, inspect the diff, then publish through Section 4.C.

### F. Mandatory 5-Stage Validation Gatekeeper & Pre-Output Self-Audit

Before delivering code or releasing a Pull Request, pass all five stages with concrete proof: (1) principal architectural review (flaws, coupling, anti-patterns, partial-failure corruption); (2) AppSec sweep (SQL injection, command injection, path traversal, XSS, CSRF, broken authentication/authorization, cross-tenant access, unsafe deserialization, sensitive data exposure, insecure dependencies); (3) performance and clean code ($O(N^2)$, needless loops, unindexed queries, leaks, dead code, cyclomatic complexity, naming); (4) QA test truthfulness and edge cases (failure paths, boundaries, races, invalid inputs; implement the mandatory unit or integration tests whose assertions prove the new behavior, not mock echoes); (5) strict specification alignment with the operator's requirements and the prohibitions of Section 5.

**Pre-output self-audit (fail-closed):** before emitting any response, patch, or review, answer internally — (1) is the code 100% complete, with zero `TODO`s, elisions, or unverified APIs? (2) are types strict, error paths fail-fast, failure paths atomic? (3) is the diff surgical, free of debris, $O(N^2)$ traps, and comment noise? (4) were security boundaries, Entire checkpoint links, and the `LCV-517` signature and handshake requirements verified? (5) is the response free of filler, praise, and hedging ("maybe", "perhaps", "consider")? (6) is operator-facing communication in pt-BR (`DD/MM/AAAA HH:MM:SS`) following the explanation rule of Section 1? Any "no" halts and rewrites.

In every repository touched, inspect failed, canceled, stuck, or missing workflow runs and cron failures ([workflow runs API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs)), and verify provenance: SSH `-S` on the branch commits of each PR, `verification.verified == true` on the GitHub-signed squash commits of `main`, and the `Entire-Checkpoint` lines carried into each squash commit (Section 4.C, Step 5).
* **External Actions updates:** keep every external Action at its current official stable version, full-SHA pinned with a version comment, through the sweep of Section 6.E and the flow of Section 4.C; each `dependabot.yml` keeps a `cooldown` configured but excludes every dependency from it (`*` inside each `package-ecosystem` block), so updates are proposed immediately; re-enabling a delay per pattern is a deliberate `exclude` edit ([Dependabot cooldown](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference#cooldown-)); updates go in SSH-signed PRs on `<agent>/...` branches unless a canonical Dependabot PR exists.
* **Wrangler compliance:** in every repository or workspace declaring `wrangler`, compare the lockfile version with the live npm registry ([npm view](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/commands/npm-view/)); if outdated, update the pin, regenerate the lockfile in the no-code mode of Section 3 and `worker-configuration.d.ts` under its Wrangler exception, commit with SSH on the branch, run the Section 4.C flow, and confirm post-merge in the deployment log: `"No wrangler version specified, using pre-installed wrangler version <x>"`.

### B. Security, Quality & Asynchronous Licensing
* **Security posture:** verify CodeQL, Secret Scanning, Zizmor, and OpenSSF Scorecard on touched repositories according to their live visibility ([code security](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security)).
* **Asynchronous native licensing:** fetch the SBOM through the asynchronous flow, `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependency-graph/sbom/generate-report` then `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependency-graph/sbom/fetch-report/{sbom_uuid}` (the synchronous endpoint is being retired, [SBOM endpoints](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/dependency-graph/sboms)), with REST API version `2026-03-10` ([API versions](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/about-the-rest-api/api-versions)); check PURLs with `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/license-compliance/package-checks`, in batches of at most 40, against that repository's policy; the API has no package check at the organization or enterprise level ([license compliance API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/dependency-graph/license-compliance)). A PURL that returns `unknown` only because of its `repository_url` qualifier is retried once without it, keeping both responses (observed behavior, `LCV-574`). The `Enterprise Open-Source License Manager` role exists since 16/10/2026 as a predefined enterprise role that reviews and approves license exception requests and receives their email notifications ([Open source license compliance](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-16-open-source-license-compliance-generally-available), [Configuring open source license policies](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/secure-your-supply-chain/manage-your-dependency-security/configure-license-policies)); it is deliberately unassigned here because the single-operator model already holds those approvals, so an audit reports `role available, not assigned`, never `role missing`. Read the live policy before any change with `GET /enterprises/{enterprise}/license-compliance/policies/default` ([REST license compliance](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/dependency-graph/license-compliance)): `PUT` on that path replaces the whole document, `licenses.allowed` and `packages` are both required and only `default` exists, so a partial body deletes existing package exceptions. Enforcement is the `license_compliance_scanning` ruleset condition, **active** on ruleset `20582436` across the fleet; an **Evaluate** ruleset annotates without blocking merges, and a branch protection rule requiring comment resolution also tracks license annotations ([About open source license compliance](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/supply-chain-security/open-source-license-compliance)).

### C. Work Intake, Triage & Routing Integrity
Query each active intake email address individually with `emailIntakeAddress(id:)`, reconstructing the live list from `emailIntakeAddressCreated` minus `emailIntakeAddressDeleted` and discarding dead IDs ([Linear GraphQL API](https://linear.app/developers/graphql)). Web forms and intake addresses route to the Team LCV Triage queue ([Linear Triage](https://linear.app/docs/triage)); intelligent triage moving items out of Triage is intentional: never disable it or move items back.

* Keep GitHub Repositories, Issues, PRs, Projects, and Releases reconciled with their Linear counterparts; never create speculative entities or link by title similarity; PR edges are many-to-many.

* **Preflight & naming:** generate a unique `RUN_KEY`, verify authentication on GitHub, Linear, Entire, and Slack, confirm no concurrent reconciliation, and acquire the shared reconciliation lock; those authentication and concurrency probes are the only external reads allowed before the lock; the first mutation after the lock renames the execution Issue to `"Auditoria diária DD/MM/AAAA — janela <início> a <fim>"` (rolling 24h window, capped at 48h if the run is delayed).

## 8. Unified Multi-Lens Code, Security & Slop Review Protocol (PRs, Trails & Local Branches)

When acting as a reviewer on a GitHub Pull Request, an Entire Trail, or a local branch, apply this protocol, which combines the LCV gates with the three Entire review lenses (`Code Review`, `Security Review`, `Slop`).

### A. Eligibility & Net Diff

1. **Dependabot hard exclusion:** inspect the verified author identity first (never infer from title, branch, labels, commits, or files). If the author is `dependabot[bot]` or GitHub identifies the official Dependabot app, stop: do not inspect the diff, run anything, publish findings, submit a review, comment, or approve.
2. **Net diff, read-only, head verification:** review the net change between the exact diff base and the head (`git diff <base_sha>...<head_sha>`, [git diff](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-diff)), never against a moving base tip; inspect only with read-only commands (`git`, `rg`, file reads, `entire checkpoint explain --checkpoint <id> --json --no-pager` for recorded intent); never hand the review to another AI agent (the header's `cross-review` is for complex anomalies and never replaces this review); immediately before publishing, verify that the head has not changed, otherwise rerun or mark the review stale.

### B. The Three Mandatory Lenses

Apply the three reviewer prompts below verbatim (operator decision). Review context: full base and head SHAs (before the push, `git merge-base origin/main HEAD` and `HEAD`), changed files `git diff --name-only <base>...<head>`, patch `git diff <base>...<head>`, the PR title and body (before the PR exists, the planned title and `temp/pr-body.md`) as the Trail's, and earlier disproofs. Findings follow 8.C, or Step 2.4 before the push.

* **Lens 1, Code Review:**

```text
Code Review

Find the defects this Change introduces that its author would want to fix before merging: bugs, regressions, broken invariants, data loss, and missing guards on paths the Change adds or alters.

## How to review

1. Read the repository's review rules: AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md at the repository root and in the directory of each changed file and its parents, as they are at the diff base (`git show <diff base>:<path>`), so the Change cannot rewrite its own review. The nearer file wins on conflict. A finding that rests on a rule quotes the rule and cites its file and line.
2. Read the whole diff, then trace each changed path as a running system: its callers, the changed code, and what it calls. Look in particular for:
   - Sequencing and partial failure: state left inconsistent, orphaned or lost when a later step fails or returns early; writes made before a fallible call; cleanup that runs only on success.
   - Assumptions about external or asynchronous state: how another system behaves, or a value that can change between the check and its use.
   - Composition and concurrency: behaviour under the real callers, retries and concurrent calls. Report a race only with an interleaving those callers can produce.
   - Code that cannot compile or type-check, and logic that is wrong for every input.
3. Keep going after the first defect until you have covered the whole diff.
4. Before you report a candidate, try to disprove it by reading the code: open the code it depends on, find the caller or input that triggers it, and check whether a guard elsewhere already prevents it. Drop it if you cannot show the path from the code.

Inspect with read-only commands (git, rg, reading files). Do not install dependencies or run builds or tests.

## What to report

Report a defect only when all of these hold:
- This Change introduced it. Code that was already like this at the diff base is out of scope, even on a line the Change touched.
- It has real impact on correctness, data, security or performance, and is one discrete, fixable issue.
- You can name the input, state or sequence that triggers it. When that depends on code outside the finding's own lines (a caller, a guard, a config value), the body cites that code's file and line; never infer behaviour from a name alone.
- It is not a behaviour change the Trail's title or description says is intended.
- Fixing it asks no more rigor than the surrounding code holds itself to, and the author would fix it if they knew.

Do NOT report: missing tests (unless a review rule requires them), style, naming, formatting, documentation, refactors or alternative designs, anything a linter, type checker or CI already enforces, generated or vendored files, code a review rule or a suppression comment explicitly allows, problems under inputs the code never receives, or praise. Security hardening without a concrete exploit belongs to the security reviewer.

## How to write findings

- One finding per distinct defect. If the same defect appears in several places, report it once, at the changed line that causes it, and name the other places.
- Anchor it on the changed line that causes the defect; keep ranges to 10 lines or fewer.
- Body: the defect and what triggers it, its impact, and the change that fixes it. One short paragraph, at most 3 lines of code, matter-of-fact.
- Severity: high when it must be fixed before merge (it breaks a real path for ordinary inputs, loses or exposes data, or opens a security hole); medium for a real defect that needs specific conditions or has limited impact; low for a real but minor defect. Never overstate it.
- Confidence: 0.9 or more when you traced the triggering path in the code; 0.7 to 0.9 with strong evidence and one assumption left; 0.5 to 0.7 when one condition could not be confirmed. Do not report anything below 0.5.
- An earlier finding is "fixed" only when the code at its location changed or the path that triggered it is gone; a commit elsewhere is not a fix.

The signal is true when you report at least one defect, new or still present, and false when you report none.
```

* **Lens 2, Security Review:**

```text
Security Review

Review this change for security vulnerabilities it introduces or exposes: missing or bypassable authentication and authorization checks, privilege escalation and cross-tenant access; injection (SQL, shell command, path traversal, template); unsafe deserialization; secrets or credentials in code, logs or errors; insecure defaults; missing validation of untrusted input at a trust boundary; and exposure of data to callers who should not see it.

Trace untrusted input from where it enters to where it is used. Report only issues with a plausible exploit path through the changed code, and state the impact.

Do NOT report: general code quality, style, missing tests, or hardening suggestions without a concrete vulnerability.

The signal is true when you report at least one vulnerability, false when you report none.
```

* **Lens 3, Slop:**

```text
Slop

You are a very strict reviewer of agent-generated code slop. Review the net change this Change introduces: the diff from its diff base to its head commit, as the review context below names it. Judge the code, not who wrote it.

The subject of the review is the final state of the diff, not the commit history. Ignore how the work was split into commits, how many pushes it took, and whether earlier commits were later fixed or reverted on the branch. A branch that arrived at a clean result through messy iteration is not slop; a branch whose final diff is sloppy is slop no matter how tidy its commits are. Anything already at the diff base is existing code, not the subject of the review.

Work from the review context:

1. Start with the changed files and the patch in the review context. For a large or truncated patch, read the rest file by file with the git diff command the review context gives, adding -- <path>.
2. Read nearby code, repo instructions, and relevant tests in the checkout to learn how the project works.
3. You may skim the commit log from the diff base to the head commit to understand intent, but do not grade individual commits.

Always review against the diff base the review context names, never the current tip of the base branch, so changes that landed on the base branch after the branch point are not attributed to this Change.

This review is read-only against the repo's own tooling. Do not install dependencies and do not run the project's build, typecheck, lint, or test commands, even to confirm something works. Judge whether tests prove the new behavior by reading the test files and the code they exercise together, the same way you already read the diff. If a test's assertions don't match what the change claims to do, that is itself the finding.

Do not run `entire review`, use other AI agents, or hand off the review. Do it yourself with the repo and local checks.

Rate the amount of **Slop** the change adds as Low, Medium, or Large. Slop is avoidable, low-trust work caused by not understanding the repo well enough. It creates extra bugs, review work, or maintenance work.

First understand what the change is trying to do. Follow every workflow, route, state change, and rule it touches from start to finish. Read whether the tests prove the new behavior instead of only matching the code or new text.

Base the rating on:

1. **Severity** — How much can the problem break or burden?
2. **Prevalence** — How much of the change has the problem?
3. **Avoidability** — Did the repo already have a simpler or established way to do it?

Look for wrong assumptions, broken flows, skipped rules, duplicate systems, weak tests, needless complexity, comment noise (comments that restate the next line, narrate what was changed and why, or explain things the repo's conventions already make obvious), leftover debris from iteration (dead code, stale comments, unused helpers, abandoned approaches), and work that is much larger than the result it delivers. Be very critical, but do not raise the rating just because the diff is large or has several small issues. Do not call necessary complexity slop, and do not charge the change for problems it merely sits next to.

Choose one:
- **Low** (signal value small): No real slop, or only small isolated issues that do not weaken the main implementation.
- **Medium** (signal value medium): A central wrong assumption, repeated low-trust work, weak checks for important behavior, or meaningful avoidable rework. The implementation can still be fixed without replacing its core.
- **Large** (signal value large): Slop is widespread, the core approach is wrong or misleading, and much of it should be rewritten or removed.

Report the rating as the signal. Its rationale must name the two strongest reasons for the rating, using concrete behavior or architecture problems, not surface-level signals. Report each concrete slop problem behind the rating as a finding anchored to the changed code it concerns.
```

### C. Publication on a Pull Request

* Publish a result for every eligible pull request, even with nothing found. To tag a finished Entire session as a review, `entire session attach <SESSION_ID> --review` (dry run first, `--force` only after the operator agrees, Section 4.C, Step 2.3).
* One inline thread per finding, anchored to the smallest changed range (≤ 10 lines) ([review comments API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/comments)); a file-level comment when no changed line fits; a pull-request-level comment with a stable identifier and exact file references when GitHub offers no valid target; never a finding only in hidden output and never an unrelated anchor.
* A pull-request-level summary for every eligible pull request with: the full base and head SHAs; Entire checkpoint intent coverage (when applicable) and the Slop Rating with its two strongest concrete reasons; checks executed, checks not executed, residual validation gaps.
* With no supported finding, the summary begins with exactly: `Review completed: no bugs, security defects, or other reportable issues were found in the reviewed changes, subject to the checks and residual validation gaps stated below.` — never silence, an emoji, an approval state, `LGTM`, or a claim about code outside the reviewed scope.
* Never secrets, credentials, unnecessary exploit payloads, or weaponization details in pull-request comments.

# Changelog

Notable changes to this repository are recorded here from 02/09/2026 onward.
Earlier work is verifiable in the commit history and in the closed pull
requests.

This repository is **not versioned**: it publishes the personal profile of
`lcv-leo` and the static site at lcv-leo.lcv.dev. It does not publish packages
or a numbered artifact. Entries are grouped by date rather than semantic
version. Dates are written `DD/MM/AAAA` in Brasília time (UTC−03:00).

## Unreleased

- Adopt the GitHub Actions workflow dependency lockfile
  (`.github/workflows/actions.lock`, generated by `gh actions-lock --no-narrow`),
  which records every action dependency at an exact commit together with the
  source repository identity, and is refreshed by Dependabot in the same pull
  request
  ([Workflow dependency lockfiles](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/workflow-dependency-lockfiles)).
  Every workflow `uses:` reference keeps its full-length commit SHA and version
  comment unchanged; the lockfile adds pinning for the three transitive Action
  revisions the workflow files cannot express (`oven-sh/setup-bun` v2.2.0,
  `actions/upload-artifact` v7.0.0 and `github/codeql-action` v4.39.3), now
  named with their commits and commit-pinned license links in the new
  `THIRDPARTY.md` subsection. The `Require lockfile` policy runs in **Evaluate**
  mode at the enterprise. This
  repository has no same-repository `uses: ./` action, so neither
  `--migrate-local-actions` nor `--ignore-local-actions` applies. `AGENTS.md`
  and `CLAUDE.md` Sections 6.E item 2 and 7.A now copy the workspace master
  text that adopts the lockfile, replacing the passages that declared it
  nonexistent or retired, and `SECURITY.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` and the
  third-party inventory carry the same rule; the inventory's license links for
  `github/codeql-action`, `zizmorcore/zizmor-action` and
  `anthropics/claude-code-action` were aligned to the pins the workflow files
  already carry (LCV-719).

- Run the official `verify-lockfile` workflow
  (`.github/workflows/verify-lockfile.yml`) on every pull request through the
  `github/gh-actions-lock` action, pinned to `verify/v0.5.1` at its full commit
  SHA. The job fails when `.github/workflows/actions.lock` is out of sync with
  the workflow files or a locked pin no longer verifies upstream, so drift is
  visible on the pull request that introduces it. The check reports and does not
  block: it is not a required check (LCV-738).

- Update Claude Code Action to v1.0.280 and Dependency Review Action to v5.0.1
  at their complete immutable release commit SHAs, preserving workflow inputs
  and permissions. Align the Claude Code Action MIT license link with its new
  pin; the bundled minimatch license change to ISC is approved under LCV-666.

- Correct the master text's Section 7.C intake-routing rule in `AGENTS.md` and
  `CLAUDE.md`: the exactly-one-Team-or-template invariant applies to addresses
  of type `team`, `template`, and `asks`; Linear's official documentation
  proves that `asksWeb` web-form addresses carry no Team/Template field by
  platform design (the form routes through its page and template, and the API
  refuses updates on them), so an `asksWeb` address with null team and null
  template is valid — never a finding or a pendency. This closes the external
  pendency that held the daily audits at PARTIAL since LCV-604, proven
  10/11/2026 under LCV-619.

- Align `.github/dependabot.yml` with the fleet standard: each `package-ecosystem`

# Third-party components

This inventory covers every external GitHub Action invoked by the repository
workflows, the CI-only npm and browser validation tooling, and the externally
hosted components used by the profile or the Pages site. The repository's
package manifest contains only development tooling for browser-level
provenance tests. No npm package, browser binary, or FFmpeg binary is copied
into `site/` or the deployed GitHub Pages artifact; the site's committed
JavaScript uses browser built-ins and GitHub APIs.

The versioned inventory is the repository's **dependency graph** (Insights →
Dependency graph), which GitHub maintains from the committed manifest, lockfile
and workflow files and exports as an SBOM on request. Versions, version ranges
and immutable commit pins for everything a workflow references directly live
only in `package.json`, `package-lock.json`, the workflow files and
`.github/workflows/actions.lock`, where Dependabot updates them; this document
does not restate those direct pins, so it can never drift from those sources.
The single exception is the transitive Action revisions that no
workflow `uses:` line points at: their exact commits are named in the
subsection under **GitHub
Actions** below, because no workflow reference records them. The
GitHub Actions dependency lockfile (`.github/workflows/actions.lock`, generated
by `gh actions-lock --no-narrow` and never edited by hand) pins those transitive
Actions and records each source repository's identity
([Workflow dependency lockfiles](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/workflow-dependency-lockfiles)).
The official GitHub
Dependency Review action evaluates manifest and lockfile changes on every pull
request to `main`, and the Pages workflow installs the committed lockfile with lifecycle
scripts disabled.

The repository's original content is proprietary and all rights are reserved.
The licenses below apply only to their respective third-party components.

## GitHub Actions

Every external Action is pinned to a full-length immutable commit SHA: the
workflow files carry their direct `uses:` references with a version comment,

records each resolved commit.

"Transitive only" because no `uses:` line references it. The subsection below
names the exact commit of each transitive dependency the lockfile records.
Tooling that an

and the CodeQL bundle used by code scanning) is governed by that Action's own
release and license; the Claude Code software itself has its own license, noted
below the table.

Enforce these rules continuously during every task, on every repository or entity touched, and whenever the full-fleet sweep runs (skill `auditoria-diaria` in `APLICAR` mode, which embeds `reconciliacao-linear-github` and `auditor-licenciamento-open-source`):
 
 ### A. GitHub Actions & Wrangler Hygiene
-* **Workflow health and provenance:** merge queue and the Actions lockfile are retired on the fleet (operator decision): never create a merge queue or a merge-group gate; Dependabot pull requests merge through repository-local automerge ([auto-merge](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/how-tos/merge-and-close-pull-requests/automatically-merging-a-pull-request)); agent pull requests follow Section 4.C. In every repository touched, inspect failed, canceled, stuck, or missing workflow runs and cron failures ([workflow runs API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs)), and verify provenance: SSH `-S` on the branch commits of each PR, `verification.verified == true` on the GitHub-signed squash commits of `main`, and the `Entire-Checkpoint` lines carried into each squash commit (Section 4.C, Step 5).
+* **Workflow health and provenance:** merge queue is retired on the fleet (operator decision): never create a merge queue or a merge-group gate. The Actions lockfile is on across the fleet (operator decision, 25/11/2026, Section 6.E, item 2): every repository commits `.github/workflows/actions.lock`, generated with `gh actions-lock --no-narrow` so the workflow `uses:` references keep their full-length commit SHA and version comment ([Workflow dependency lockfiles](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/security/workflow-dependency-lockfiles)), and an audit reports a missing or stale lockfile as a finding. Dependabot pull requests merge through repository-local automerge ([auto-merge](https://docs.github.com/en/pull-requests/how-tos/merge-and-close-pull-requests/automatically-merging-a-pull-request)); agent pull requests follow Section 4.C. In every repository touched, inspect failed, canceled, stuck, or missing workflow runs and cron failures ([workflow runs API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/actions/workflow-runs)), and verify provenance: SSH `-S` on the branch commits of each PR, `verification.verified == true` on the GitHub-signed squash commits of `main`, and the `Entire-Checkpoint` lines carried into each squash commit (Section 4.C, Step 5).
 * **External Actions updates:** keep every external Action at its current official stable version, full-SHA pinned with a version comment, through the sweep of Section 6.E and the flow of Section 4.C; each `dependabot.yml` keeps a `cooldown` configured but excludes every dependency from it (`*` inside each `package-ecosystem` block), so updates are proposed immediately; re-enabling a delay per pattern is a deliberate `exclude` edit ([Dependabot cooldown](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/reference/supply-chain-security/dependabot-options-reference#cooldown-)); updates go in SSH-signed PRs on `<agent>/...` branches unless a canonical Dependabot PR exists.
 * **Wrangler compliance:** in every repository or workspace declaring `wrangler`, compare the lockfile version with the live npm registry ([npm view](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/commands/npm-view/)); if outdated, update the pin, regenerate the lockfile in the no-code mode of Section 3 and `worker-configuration.d.ts` under its Wrangler exception, commit with SSH on the branch, run the Section 4.C flow, and confirm post-merge in the deployment log: `"No wrangler version specified, using pre-installed wrangler version <x>"`.
 
 ### B. Security, Quality & Asynchronous Licensing
 * **Security posture:** verify CodeQL, Secret Scanning, Zizmor, and OpenSSF Scorecard on touched repositories according to their live visibility ([code security](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security)).
-* **Asynchronous native licensing:** fetch the SBOM through the asynchronous flow, `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependency-graph/sbom/generate-report` then `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependency-graph/sbom/fetch-report/{sbom_uuid}` (the synchronous endpoint is being retired, [SBOM endpoints](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/dependency-graph/sboms)), with REST API version `2026-03-10` ([API versions](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/about-the-rest-api/api-versions)); check PURLs with `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/license-compliance/package-checks`, in batches of at most 40, against that repository's policy; the API has no package check at the organization or enterprise level ([license compliance API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/dependency-graph/license-compliance)). A PURL that returns `unknown` only because of its `repository_url` qualifier is retried once without it, keeping both responses (observed behavior, `LCV-574`). The absence of a separate "Enterprise Open-Source License Manager" role is not a gap (single-operator model).
+* **Asynchronous native licensing:** fetch the SBOM through the asynchronous flow, `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependency-graph/sbom/generate-report` then `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/dependency-graph/sbom/fetch-report/{sbom_uuid}` (the synchronous endpoint is being retired, [SBOM endpoints](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/dependency-graph/sboms)), with REST API version `2026-03-10` ([API versions](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/about-the-rest-api/api-versions)); check PURLs with `POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/license-compliance/package-checks`, in batches of at most 40, against that repository's policy; the API has no package check at the organization or enterprise level ([license compliance API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/dependency-graph/license-compliance)). A PURL that returns `unknown` only because of its `repository_url` qualifier is retried once without it, keeping both responses (observed behavior, `LCV-574`). The `Enterprise Open-Source License Manager` role exists since 16/10/2026 as a predefined enterprise role that reviews and approves license exception requests and receives their email notifications ([Open source license compliance](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-10-16-open-source-license-compliance-generally-available), [Configuring open source license policies](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/secure-your-supply-chain/manage-your-dependency-security/configure-license-policies)); it is deliberately unassigned here because the single-operator model already holds those approvals, so an audit reports `role available, not assigned`, never `role missing`. Read the live policy before any change with `GET /enterprises/{enterprise}/license-compliance/policies/default` ([REST license compliance](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/dependency-graph/license-compliance)): `PUT` on that path replaces the whole document, `licenses.allowed` and `packages` are both required and only `default` exists, so a partial body deletes existing package exceptions. Enforcement is the `license_compliance_scanning` ruleset condition, **active** on ruleset `20582436` across the fleet; an **Evaluate** ruleset annotates without blocking merges, and a branch protection rule requiring comment resolution also tracks license annotations ([About open source license compliance](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/supply-chain-security/open-source-license-compliance)).
 
 ### C. Work Intake, Triage & Routing Integrity
 Query each active intake email address individually with `emailIntakeAddress(id:)`, reconstructing the live list from `emailIntakeAddressCreated` minus `emailIntakeAddressDeleted` and discarding dead IDs ([Linear GraphQL API](https://linear.app/developers/graphql)). Each active address of type `team`, `template`, or `asks` links to exactly one Team or one template (dual targets are a finding); for a template, verify `templateData.teamId`, falling back to the template's own Team. An address of type `asksWeb` has no team and no template, because its destination comes from the Asks web settings (`EmailIntakeAddress.team` in the Linear GraphQL API); null team and null template are valid there, never a finding or a pendency. Web forms and intake addresses route to the Team LCV Triage queue ([Linear Triage](https://linear.app/docs/triage)); intelligent triage moving items out of Triage is intentional: never disable it or move items back.
